items.title: WeKaribu
lines: The host hears it in hers.
items.foot: Hack-Nation × World Bank · Small AI for Development · Tourism
items.text: WeKaribu. Because of this tool, Noor, a coffee-farm host in Tanzania, will hear in Swahili what her visitors loved and what to improve. Today she never does: the feedback is in languages she cannot read.

items.title: A friend’s tip is enough
items.text: A friend's tip is enough: the search locks on Noor's farm. Vivian books a day Noor published and pays the deposit by M-Pesa, straight to Noor's phone.

items.title: Noor decides
items.text: Noor accepts: the final call is hers, by app or by SMS. After the visit, a guestbook photo in German and a French voice note are read and translated on the phone, offline.

items.title: The week, in Swahili
items.text: Ten fixed topics, good or bad; anything unsure is flagged for a person. The summary is human-written Swahili the AI only fills in, and Noor can listen to it.

items.title: A thank-you, with consent
items.text: SMS can carry the words; only a model can carry the meaning. Nothing is sent without Noor's tap. WeKaribu: we welcome.
